name: Chilopsis

project_scope.note: One canonical species in this genus in the current learner; comparisons to other genera are NOT separate canonical species.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Free-standing deciduous shrub/small tree, not a climbing vine. Leaves simple and extraordinarily narrow, alternate OR opposite on different shoots; long, ruffled pink-lavender trumpet flowers; extremely long thin dry two-valved capsules release flat seeds with hair-fringed ends. It is NOT a true Salix willow.
shared_genus_recognition.emphasis: USE LEAF STRUCTURE / CLIMBING MECHANISM first; flower color alone is poor Bignoniaceae ID. Confirm with long 2-valved capsule and seeds.
shared_genus_recognition.family_note: Bignoniaceae generally has bilateral trumpet-shaped flowers with four fertile didynamous stamens + reduced fifth, and capsules with winged or haired seeds.

look_here_first_sequence: First decide that the plant is a SELF-SUPPORTING small tree, not a vine; this splits from local Campsis/Bignonia.
Inspect a simple, extremely narrow leaf (often alternate, sometimes opposite); no individual leaflets or tendrils.
Examine flowering twigs for broad-throated ruffled flowers marked with streaks rather than willow catkins.
On fruiting specimens examine long, narrow two-valved capsules and flattened seed fringes, unlike Salix cottony seed plumes.
lookalikes_and_scientific_cautions: True willows (Salix spp., Salicaceae) produce catkins and capsules with tufted silky seeds; do not key Chilopsis by narrow leaves alone.
Catalpa and ×Chitalpa hybrids are Bignoniaceae with showy flowers and capsules, but foliage and parentage differ; garden provenance matters.
Chilopsis linearis occurs naturally in arid western/southwestern Texas and is planted elsewhere; canonical target-zone native status remains false.
Simple leaves may be alternate, opposite or sometimes whorled; a family key requiring opposite compound foliage will incorrectly exclude Chilopsis.

simple linear leaf vs pinnate vs tendrilled leaves, clear labels
